feat(scheduling): pgqueuer durable-execution pilot for human_systems_scheduler (USS-TJR-MSN-0375)

Replaces human_systems_scheduler.py's BlockingScheduler/CronTrigger daemon
with pgqueuer (Postgres-native SKIP LOCKED queue, existing Supabase
instance, zero new infra) to close the disclosed double-fire risk on the
Scheduling capability. Preserves JOBS/_CRON_DEFAULTS/_JOB_DOMAIN and all
env-var cron overrides unchanged.

Stream 0 found this daemon has never had production supervision anywhere
in the repo (no service/timer/crontab/tmux reference) -- added
deploy/human-systems-scheduler.service to close that gap; not yet
installed on the production VM (needs a new SUPABASE_DB_URL secret).

Demonstrated the double-fire scenario directly: a naive concurrent claim
(the APScheduler-shaped race) double-fires (run_count=2); the same race
against pgqueuer's FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED dequeue executes exactly once,
with a queryable pgqueuer_log/pgqueuer_schedules ledger as evidence. A
live smoke test of the real _start_daemon_async() wiring (not a copy)
against a local Postgres confirmed all 7 jobs register with their correct
env-var cron expressions and dispatch correctly.

Corrected SUOC Platform Registry's Scheduling capability: the long-standing
"5 fragmented apscheduler instances" claim does not survive a direct grep
-- only 3 real independent scheduler processes exist. Recommends an
incremental Wave-4 migration (human_systems_scheduler.py done here;
intelligence/scheduler.py deferred to a dedicated future mission given its
blast radius; revs/scheduler.py lowest priority, already partially
protected). intelligence/scheduler.py, revs/scheduler.py, deploy/*.timer,
and the Task Engine are untouched per this pilot's scope.

See knowledge/missions/USS-TJR-MSN-0375-knowledge-record.md for full
detail (bake-off vs procrastinate, dedup proof output, go/no-go).

Attestation: no production access from this sandbox -- Stream 0's ground
truth is a repo-search finding (absence of any service/timer/crontab
reference), not a live-host check. Stream 1's wiring was verified against
a local Postgres via Docker (real pgqueuer code, monkeypatched run_job --
no Supabase/Telegram creds available here), not the production Supabase
instance. Stream 3's dedup demonstration ran against real Postgres/real
pgqueuer library code, output captured in the knowledge record. Not yet
deployed; deploy/human-systems-scheduler.service is new and unenabled.
